episodes.182130: Afternoon storms over the Sangre de Cristo Mountains slowly moved south across the Hermits Peak Calf Canyon Burn Scar resulting in some flash flooding at Lower Rociada.
episodes.182581: A stalled frontal boundary across the Midlands and CSRA was the focus for some strong to severe thunderstorms across the eastern Midlands, mainly Clarendon County.
episodes.182660: Abundant subtropical moisture paired with weak steering flow resulted in slow moving showers and thunderstorms across the higher terrain of western Colorado. Some of the stronger storms produced heavy rain which led to debris flows in portions of Garfield County, including on the Grizzly Creek Fire burn scar in Glenwood Canyon. Flooding also occurred in portions of Moffat County due to heavy rain from storms.
episodes.183106: Thunderstorms pushing offshore produced strong wind gusts in the Indian River near Cape Canaveral.
episodes.183641: A strong thunderstorm produced a funnel cloud and minor wind gust damage in Mayaguez on the 16th of August.
episodes.183844: Unsettled southwest flow continued rounds of showers and thunderstorms with a surface trough lingering over Georgia and passing mid-level short wave troughs from the |WSW enhancing rounds of convection near low level convergence. Deep layer moisture with PWAT 2+ inches was under fairly weak WSW steering flow of < 10 kts and continued the localized heavy rainfall threat, especially during the afternoon toward the Atlantic |coast where the east coast sea breeze developed and across SE GA near the meandering surface front.

Deep layer moisture with PWAT 2+ inches was under fairly weak WSW steering flow of < 10 kts and continued the localized heavy rainfall threat, especially during the afternoon toward the Atlantic|coast where the east coast sea breeze developed and across SE GA near the meandering surface front.
episodes.184086: An upper level low pressure system with weak winds and high levels of deep moisture pooling along a weak surface trough resulted in clusters of slow moving thunderstorms over Monroe County during the pre-dawn hours. These storms produced very heavy rain with multiple instances of flash flooding reported across the Rochester Metro. Top rainfall reports included; 3.13 inches at the Rochester Airport, 3.00 inches near Greece and 2.84 inches on the northwest side of Rochester.
episodes.184128: The combination of strong daytime heating and orographic lifting along terrain features led to the development of isolated thunderstorms across south-central AZ during the afternoon hours on the 17th. Moderate instability in place with MLCAPE of approximately 1000 J/KG was sufficient for some of these thunderstorms to become strong as was the case with the storm that developed off the Estrellas Mountains located just southwest of downtown Phoenix and led to a 68 mph measured gust from a mesonet station located at the Phoenix International Raceway in Avondale.
episodes.184149: A series of repeated heavy rain events in Anchorage caused flooding in various areas of the city.  Each event caused additional severity of impacts as the ground and streams did not have sufficient time to dry out before the next heavy rain event.
episodes.184630: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184633: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184693: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.184725: Persistent shower and thunderstorm activity affected portions of eastern Essex County, NY  during the afternoon of August 16, 2023. The towns of Moriah and Westport received between one and three inches of rain leading to a few areas of flash flooding.
episodes.184802: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 16th across northwest Wisconsin ahead of a cold front. Daytime heating led to strong instability over the region and a strong low level jet provided ample wind shear for storms to work with. With the cold front, the storms were generally linear in mode resulting in damaging winds being the primary threat as they moved to the east. Numerous reports of tree damage were received from across northwest Wisconsin into the evening hours along with a few hail reports. The largest hail report was half dollar-sized.
episodes.184807: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 16th across far northeastern Minnesota ahead of a cold front. Daytime heating led to strong instability over the region and a strong low level jet provided ample wind shear for storms to work with. With the cold front, the storms were generally linear in mode resulting in strong wind guts as they moved over portions of western Lake Superior.
episodes.184998: A weak upper level trough interacted with moisture and instability over south Texas to produce scattered thunderstorms in the afternoon. Storms produced wind damage over southern Bee and western San Patricio Counties near the communities of Tynan and West Sinton.
episodes.185045: The combination of warm and moist conditions occurring ahead of a cold front approaching from the west along with forcing associated with a sea breeze circulation shifting inland led to strong thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds across southeast Georgia.
episodes.185046: The combination of warm and moist conditions occurring ahead of a cold front arriving during the night led to strong thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds across coastal waters.
episodes.185083: A line of thunderstorms impacted the Coastal Plain, the inland sounds, and rivers during the evening hours on the 15th. Some of the storms embedded within this line were strong to severe in nature bringing strong wind gusts to the Albemarle and Pamlico Sounds, as well as the Neuse river.
episodes.185447: An isolated waterspout was observed offshore Key West in association with a convective shower.  A mid-altitude cyclonic circulation was noted over the western Straits of Florida and western Cuba.
episodes.185560: Waterspout observed west of Boca Grande with evening thunderstorms.
episodes.189477: A narrow waterspout developed off the south shore of Key West, and moved north, making landfall as a tornado at Higgs Beach of Key West.
episodes.192660: Several places around Zion National Park had flooding as monsoonal showers and thunderstorm tracked there.

Heavy rain led to flooded creeks and streams across Anchorage, reaching up to moderate flood levels; overflows impacted nearby properties in Anchorage. Up to 2 inches of rain fell within 6 hours (with 1.27 inches reported in 1 hour by a trained spotter) on already saturated soils and already elevated streamflows August 16. This caused aerial flooding along roadways and streams in a short span of time across widespread areas of downtown Anchorage, as well as along Chester Creek. ||At 3AM, deep water at 20th and Bragaw caused cars to get stranded; 3 ft of water at 12th and Cordova led to water infiltration of ground level apartments.

events.narrative: A narrow waterspout was observed directly south of Key West in Hawk Channel.  The condensation cloud extended all the way down to the water surface with a spray ring extending approximately one-quarter the way up the condensation funnel.  The waterspout was observed to move onshore near Higgs beach and quickly dissipated without any discernable impact nor damage.

A narrow waterspout with a spray ring extending one-quarter the way up from the water surface to cloud base moved north onshore Higgs Beach as a tornado.  The tornado dissipated on the beach without any discernable damage noted.  Maximum wind speeds of 50 to 60 mph were estimated at the landfall location.
